places.name: Fisherman’s Bastion
places.desc: Fairytale towers, sweeping river views and the streets of old Buda.
places.body: Explore the terraces overlooking the Danube, then wander towards Matthias Church and the quiet streets of the Castle District. The lower walkways and the upper lookout have different access arrangements; check current admission details before visiting.

places.name: Hungarian Parliament
places.desc: Meet the city’s riverside landmark, from Kossuth Square to the opposite bank.
places.body: Start with the exterior on Kossuth Square, then follow the Pest riverfront for a different perspective. For an interior visit, use the official visitor service to check current tours and ticket availability. A walk on the Buda bank gives you the full riverside view.

places.name: The Danube panorama
places.time: Best enjoyed at your own pace
places.desc: Two riverbanks, beautiful bridges and a whole new perspective on the city.
places.body: Make the river your starting point. Explore the embankments, cross between Buda and Pest and pause for views of the Parliament and Castle Hill. A sightseeing cruise is another way to experience the river; check routes, departure points and accessibility with the operator.

places.name: Széchenyi Thermal Bath
places.desc: A thermal-bath experience to pair with a slower day in City Park.
places.body: Set aside time for one of Budapest’s best-known thermal-bath experiences, then explore City Park nearby. Bring swimwear and check current age restrictions, pool access, opening hours and ticket conditions directly with the bath before booking.

places.name: Matthias Church
places.desc: Patterned roof tiles and an atmospheric stop in the heart of the Castle District.
places.body: Take time to notice the colourful roof and the details around Holy Trinity Square. Combine the church with the nearby Bastion for a relaxed Buda morning. Worship and visitor access can have different schedules; confirm current visiting information with the church.

places.name: Buda Castle District
places.desc: Historic streets, courtyards and viewpoints above the river.
places.body: Treat Castle Hill as a neighbourhood to explore slowly. Start around Matthias Church and Fisherman’s Bastion, then continue towards the palace area. Expect slopes and some uneven surfaces. Check individual museums and venues separately before a visit.

river: Walk a stretch of the riverfront, look across to Parliament and leave time to stop. For a cruise, compare the route, departure pier, duration and what is included directly with the operator. This first version of GoToBudapest does not process tour bookings.
bath: Build a slower day around a thermal-bath visit. Széchenyi pairs naturally with City Park. Check current age rules, pool access and ticket conditions directly with the bath before visiting. Bring swimwear and confirm any other equipment requirements.
food: Start with a market visit, then leave room for a café stop. Look for Hungarian dishes such as gulyás, lángos and chimney cake. Check menus and dietary information directly with each venue; opening hours vary. Pair your food stops with a walk through downtown Pest.
basics: The local currency is the Hungarian forint (HUF). Keep your accommodation address available offline. Use the official BKK website or BudapestGO for current public-transport information. Castle Hill has slopes and cobbled stretches, so plan for your mobility needs. Confirm opening hours directly with venues.
